sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The **Famous Books & Authors** (प्रसिद्ध पुस्तकें एवं लेखक) static general awareness section under **UPSSSC PET** syllabus.
Covers ancient classical texts, medieval Persian/Sanskrit chronicles, modern Indian literature, and contemporary global literature.
Questions originate from national curricula, historical milestones, international literary awards, and prominent political autobiographies.
Curated for aspirants targeting **Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission** Preliminary Eligibility Test.
Carries **1 to 2 guaranteed marks** in the General Awareness section of UPSSSC PET with direct, factual queries.
Categorized into Ancient Indian Authors, Medieval Chronicles, Freedom Fighters' Works, Modern Indian Authors, and International Best-sellers.
High-scoring, low-effort area requiring rote memorization of author-book pairings, pen names, and award-winning novels.
Frequently features winners of the **Booker Prize**, **Jnanpith Award**, **Sahitya Akademi Award**, and classic Sanskrit plays.

items.title: Ancient Indian Literature & Classical Texts
items.content:
• **Kautilya (Chanakya):** Authored **Arthashastra**, a masterclass on statecraft and economic policy.
• **Kalidasa:** Celebrated poet of the Gupta period; wrote **Meghaduta**, **Abhijnanashakuntalam**, **Raghuvamsa**, and **Kumarasambhava**.
• **Banabhatta:** Court poet of King Harsha; authored **Harshacharita** and **Kadambari**.
• **Vishnu Sharma:** Wrote **Panchatantra**, the world's most translated collection of fables.
• **Mnemonic:** **KVB** = **K**alidasa, **V**ishnu Sharma, **B**anabhatta make ancient books **B**est **S**ellers (**M**eghaduta, **P**anchatantra, **H**arshacharita).

items.title: Medieval Chronicles & Persian Literature
items.content:
• **Firdausi:** Authored **Shahnama** (Book of Kings).
• **Al-Biruni:** Authored **Kitab-ul-Hind** (Tarikh-ul-Hind), detailing 11th-century India.
• **Amir Khusrow:** Known as the Parrot of India; wrote **Nihpr-us-Siphr** and **Khazain-ul-Futuh**.
• **Abul Fazl:** Court historian of Akbar; wrote **Akbarnama** and **Ain-i-Akbari**.
• **Gulbadan Begum:** Authored **Humayun-nama**, chronicling the reign of Emperor Humayun.

items.title: Indian Freedom Struggle & Nationalist Literature
items.content:
• **Mahatma Gandhi:** Authored **My Experiments with Truth** and **Hind Swaraj**.
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:** Authored **Discovery of India**, **Glimpses of World History**, and **An Autobiography**.
• **Rabindranath Tagore:** Authored **Gitanjali** (won Nobel Prize in 1913), **Gora**, and **Hungry Stones**.
• **Bankim Chandra Chatterjee:** Authored **Anandamath** (source of National Song Vande Mataram) and **Durgeshnandini**.
• **Subhash Chandra Bose:** Authored **The Indian Struggle**.

items.title: Modern Indian Authors & Literary Awards
items.content:
• **Arundhati Roy:** Won the Booker Prize in **1997** for **The God of Small Things**.
• **Chetan Bhagat:** Authored pop-fiction hits like **Five Point Someone** and **2 States**.
• **R.K. Narayan:** Created the fictional town of Malgudi; authored **Swami and Friends** and **The Guide**.
• **Khushwant Singh:** Authored **Train to Pakistan**.
• **Mnemonic:** **ARK** = **A**rundhati Roy (**G**od of Small Things), **R**.K. Narayan (**G**uide), **K**hushwant Singh (**T**rain to Pakistan).

items.title: World Literature & International Classics
items.content:
• **William Shakespeare:** Authored **Hamlet**, **Macbeth**, **Romeo and Juliet**, and **Othello**.
• **Leo Tolstoy:** Authored **War and Peace** and **Anna Karenina**.
• **Charles Dickens:** Authored **A Tale of Two Cities** and **Oliver Twist**.
• **George Orwell:** Authored **1984** and **Animal Farm**.
• **J.K. Rowling:** Authored the fantasy series **Harry Potter**.

items.definition: Remember Nehru's major books using the acronym **D-G-A**: **D**iscovery of India, **G**limpses of World History, and **A**n Autobiography. All written or conceptualized during his imprisonment.
Mahatma Gandhi's ideological and personal works: **My Experiments with Truth** (personal autobiography) and **Hind Swaraj** (political/ideological blueprint).
Group Kalidasa's works into **3 Dramas** (Malavikagnimitram, Vikramorvasiyam, Abhijnanashakuntalam) and **2 Epics** (Raghuvamsa, Kumarasambhava) plus **2 Lyric Poems** (Meghaduta, Ritusamhara).
Recall Indian Booker winners using the sequence: **Arundhati Roy** (1997) -> **Kiran Desai** (2006) -> **Aravind Adiga** (2008) -> **Geetanjali Shree** (International Booker 2022 for Tomb of Sand).
Key Tagore works to remember: **Gitanjali** (Nobel 1913), **Gora** (social novel), **Kabuliwala** (short story), and **Jana Gana Mana** (National Anthem).

items.term: Trick 6: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam's Autographical Works
items.definition: Kalam's inspirational trio: **Wings of Fire** (autobiography), **Ignited Minds**, and **India 2020: A Vision for the New Millennium**.
Students often assume Emperor Humayun wrote **Humayun-nama**. Correct fact: It was written by his sister, **Gulbadan Begum**, on the orders of Emperor Akbar.
Students confuse separate authors. Both **Akbarnama** and **Ain-i-Akbari** were written by **Abul Fazl**, where Ain-i-Akbari is technically the third volume of Akbarnama.

items.term: Mistake 3: Confusing National Song and National Anthem Books
items.definition: Remember that **Anandamath** (Bankim Chandra Chatterjee) contains the National Song (**Vande Mataram**), whereas **Gitanjali** / Jana Gana Mana lyrics are by **Rabindranath Tagore**.

items.term: Mistake 4: Booker Prize vs International Booker Prize
items.definition: Do not confuse **Arundhati Roy** (won Booker Prize in 1997 for English fiction) with **Geetanjali Shree** (won **International Booker Prize** in 2022 for translated Hindi novel *Tomb of Sand* / *Ret Samadhi*).

items.term: Mistake 5: Panini vs Kautilya Subject Matter
items.definition: Students mix up **Panini** (grammar in *Ashtadhyayi*) with **Kautilya** (statecraft in *Arthashastra*). Associate **P**anini with **P**rincipal Grammar.
Key books include **Arthashastra** by Chanakya, **Ashtadhyayi** by Panini, **Indica** by Megasthenes, and **Meghaduta** by Kalidasa.
Essential texts comprise **Kitab-ul-Hind** by Al-Biruni, **Shahnama** by Firdausi, **Akbarnama** by Abul Fazl, and **Humayun-nama** by Gulbadan Begum.

Crucial books include **Hind Swaraj** by Mahatma Gandhi, **Discovery of India** by Jawaharlal Nehru, **Anandamath** by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, and **Poverty and Un-British Rule in India** by Dadabhai Naoroji.

Prominent award winners include **Gitanjali** by Rabindranath Tagore (Nobel 1913), **The God of Small Things** by Arundhati Roy (Booker 1997), and **Tomb of Sand** by Geetanjali Shree (International Booker 2022).
Must-know works include **Wings of Fire** by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, **The Guide** by R.K. Narayan, **Train to Pakistan** by Khushwant Singh, and **Five Point Someone** by Chetan Bhagat.
Important international books include **War and Peace** by Leo Tolstoy, **Hamlet** by William Shakespeare, **1984** by George Orwell, and **Les Miserables** by Victor Hugo.

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET frequently asks matching-type questions where four books are matched with four authors. Focus heavily on matching classical Sanskrit texts and freedom fighter autobiographies.
Make a dedicated flashcard list for recent Indian winners of prestigious literary awards like the Jnanpith Award, Sahitya Akademi Award, and Booker Prize.
Examiners often swap medieval chronicle authors (e.g., attributing Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi to the wrong Sultan or historian like Ziauddin Barani). Verify the author's exact name.
Do not confuse English translations of Indian vernacular novels with original titles; UPSSSC PET often uses original Hindi/Bengali titles like *Ret Samadhi* or *Anandamath*.

keyTakeaways: Kautilya's **Arthashastra** and Panini's **Ashtadhyayi** are foundational ancient Indian texts frequently tested in UPSSSC PET.
Abul Fazl (**Akbarnama**) and Gulbadan Begum (**Humayun-nama**) represent crucial medieval historiography questions.
Mahatma Gandhi (**Hind Swaraj**) and Jawaharlal Nehru (**Discovery of India**) form the core of freedom struggle literature.
Rabindranath Tagore's **Gitanjali** secured Asia's first Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
Geetanjali Shree's **Tomb of Sand** (*Ret Samadhi*) is a milestone modern book as the first Hindi novel to win the International Booker Prize.
Always cross-verify author names for historical biographies to avoid confusion between the subject and the actual writer.
